commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config

Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

## Mistral OCR on Azure AI Foundry

Mistral OCR is a state-of-the-art Optical Character Recognition (OCR) model launched in the Azure AI Foundry model catalog that brings intelligent document understanding to a whole new level. It is designed for speed, precision, and multilingual versatility.

## Key Vision and Language Capabilities

Mistral Document AI combines vision + language understanding to interpret complex page layouts. Instead of receiving only raw text from OCR, you obtain markdown plus optional structured annotations that preserve tables, headings, figures, and multilingual content.

Compared to traditional OCR approaches, it maintains structural semantics: tables remain tables, figures are preserved, headings stay delineated, and mathematical or LaTeX elements are not flattened into ambiguous text.

## Supported Formats and Languages

The model supports 25+ languages and handles PDFs and images (including scanned, mixed‑content pages) with high accuracy.

## Azure Integration Benefits

Mistral Document AI is available as a serverless model in Azure AI Foundry and brings multimodal, layout‑aware document understanding directly into a developer workflow without provisioning GPUs. Running Mistral Document AI inside Azure AI Foundry provides regional data residency as documents are processed inside your selected Azure region, and data is not forwarded to external third‑party endpoints beyond Azure's managed hosting.

input.prompt: What is the API endpoint and how do I call Mistral OCR on Azure?

content.content:
# Azure AI OCR (Mistral) API Endpoint

Based on the documentation, here's how to call Mistral OCR on Azure:

## API Endpoint
The provider route is `azure_ai/` with the model identifier `mistral-document-ai-2505`.

## Quick Implementation

Using the LiteLLM SDK, you can call the OCR service like this:

```python
import litellm
import os

os.environ["AZURE_AI_API_KEY"] = "your-key"
os.environ["AZURE_AI_API_BASE"] = "your-base-url"

response = litellm.ocr(
    model="azure_ai/mistral-document-ai-2505",
    document={
        "type": "document_url",
        "document_url": "https://example.com/document.pdf"
    }
)

for page in response.pages:
    print(page.text)
```

## Key Details

- **Supported input types**: PDFs, images, and base64-encoded documents
- **Response structure**: Includes extracted text organized by pages
- **Important note**: "Azure AI OCR endpoints don't have internet access. LiteLLM automatically converts public URLs to base64 data URIs before sending requests."
- **Async support**: Use `await litellm.aocr()` for asynchronous operations

content.text:
Yes, **Mistral OCR is available on Azure**, but not through the traditional Azure Cognitive Services endpoint you're calling.

## The Issue

The endpoint `https://<project>.cognitiveservices.azure.com/v1/ocr` is for Azure Cognitive Services' built-in OCR, not Mistral's. That's why you're getting a 404.

## Using Mistral OCR on Azure

Mistral OCR is available through **Azure AI Foundry** as a serverless deployment with the model identifier `mistral-document-ai-2505`. You need to:

1. **Access it via Azure AI Foundry**, not the standard Cognitive Services endpoint
2. Use the appropriate Azure AI Foundry API endpoint with your credentials
3. Call it with documents (PDFs, images, or base64-encoded content)

The key advantage over traditional OCR is that Mistral Document AI combines vision + language understanding to preserve document structure (tables, headings, figures) and supports 25+ languages with structured output.

## Getting Started

Refer to the official Azure AI Foundry documentation and the Mistral model catalog entry to configure your endpoint and credentials. The model integrates directly into Azure with data residency—documents stay within your Azure region.

Sources:
- [Mistral OCR on Azure AI Foundry - Microsoft Community Hub](https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/blog/azure-ai-foundry-blog/unlocking-document-intelligence-mistral-ocr-now-available-in-azure-ai-foundry/4401836)
- [Mistral OCR 25.03 - Azure AI Catalog](https://ai.azure.com/catalog/models/mistral-ocr-2503)
- [Azure AI OCR (Mistral) - liteLLM Documentation](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/providers/azure_ocr)
- [Mistral Document AI on Azure - TypeScript Guide](https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/blog/azuredevcommunityblog/unlock-structured-ocr-in-typescript-with-mistral-document-ai-on-ai-foundry/4466039)
